clues.clue: The borough's name comes from the Dutch 'Staaten Eylandt,' honoring this governing body of the Netherlands.
clues.reveal: States General. 'Staaten Eylandt' was named for the States-General, the Dutch parliament.

clues.clue: This Italian explorer sailed through the Narrows in 1524, the first European to reach the island.
clues.reveal: Verrazzano. Giovanni da Verrazzano sailed through the Narrows in 1524; the bridge to Brooklyn now bears his name.

clues.clue: Staten Island is coextensive with this county, named for a Duke of Richmond.
clues.reveal: Richmond. Staten Island is coextensive with Richmond County; the borough was officially 'Richmond' until 1975.

clues.clue: This free boat connects CB1's St. George terminal to Lower Manhattan with famous harbor views.
clues.reveal: Staten Island Ferry (CB1). The free ferry between St. George and Manhattan, with views of the Statue of Liberty.
clues.app_title: Staten Island CB1 on the app

clues.clue: Completed in 1964, this bridge linked Staten Island to Brooklyn and reshaped the borough.
clues.reveal: Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge. The 1964 span to Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, triggered Staten Island's suburban growth.

clues.clue: CB1's most urban area, this North Shore neighborhood holds the ferry terminal and Borough Hall.
clues.reveal: St. George (CB1). The civic and transit hub of the North Shore, home to the ferry terminal and Borough Hall.
clues.app_title: Staten Island CB1 on the app

clues.clue: Opened in 1948 in CB3, this site was once the world's largest landfill, now becoming a park.
clues.reveal: Fresh Kills (CB3). Once the world's largest landfill, now being transformed into Freshkills Park.
clues.app_title: Staten Island CB3 on the app

clues.clue: This restored 19th-century village in CB2 preserves Staten Island's colonial past as 'Historic' this town.
clues.reveal: Richmond Town (CB2). Historic Richmond Town is a restored village museum preserving the island's colonial history.
clues.app_title: Staten Island CB2 on the app

clues.clue: Feeling neglected by City Hall, Staten Island voters backed a 1990s movement to do this.
clues.reveal: Secede. Frustration with City Hall fueled a 1990s secession movement that won strong local support in referendums.

clues.clue: Before Europeans, the island was home to the Raritan band of these Indigenous people.
clues.reveal: Lenape. The Raritan band of the Lenape lived on the island, with seasonal camps and oyster harvesting.

clues.clue: CB3's Tottenville holds Burial Ridge, the largest pre-European one of these sites in the city.
clues.reveal: Burial Ground (CB3). Burial Ridge in Tottenville is the largest known pre-European Native American burial ground in New York City.
clues.app_title: Staten Island CB3 on the app

clues.clue: The Dutch purchased the island from the Lenape around this decade in the 1600s.
clues.reveal: 1630s. The Dutch bought Staten Island from the Lenape around 1630, though permanent settlement took decades.
